sentence: This railway station ___ in 1890.
setupText: Choose the form reporting the building's construction in the past.
taskText: This railway station ___ in 1890.
text: Choose the form reporting the building's construction in the past. This railway station ___ in 1890.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-a2-2301:Past passive in a building history
explanation: Was built is past passive: people built the station in the finished year 1890.

rationales.built: Built alone would make the station the builder; the station receives the construction action.
rationales.was building: Was building is active continuous and would describe the station doing construction.
rationales.has built: Has built is active, not passive, and does not fit this dated construction event.
rationales.was built: Was built is past passive: people built the station in the finished year 1890.

sentence: The shop did not accept my old notes.
setupText: Choose the passive sentence preserving the original negative meaning.
taskText: The shop did not accept my old notes.
text: Choose the passive sentence preserving the original negative meaning. The shop did not accept my old notes.
options: My old notes accepted the shop.
My old notes were not accepted by the shop.
My old notes were accepted by the shop.
The shop was not accepted by my old notes.
answer: My old notes were not accepted by the shop.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-a2-2302:Preserving negation in an active-to-passive paraphrase
explanation: The notes remain the things the shop refused, and were not accepted preserves the negative meaning.

rationales.My old notes were not accepted by the sh: The notes remain the things the shop refused, and were not accepted preserves the negative meaning.
This makes the notes the actor and changes what the shop did.
Removing not reverses the original refusal into acceptance.
rationales.The shop was not accepted by my old note: This reverses the roles: the original shop assessed the notes, not the other way around.

sentence: A porter carried our luggage to the taxi.
setupText: Choose the sentence that focuses on the luggage and keeps the same event.
taskText: A porter carried our luggage to the taxi.
text: Choose the sentence that focuses on the luggage and keeps the same event. A porter carried our luggage to the taxi.
options: Our luggage was carried to the taxi by a porter.
Our luggage was carried from the taxi by a porter.
Our luggage carried a porter to the taxi.
A porter was carried to the taxi with our luggage.
answer: Our luggage was carried to the taxi by a porter.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-a2-2303:Passive paraphrase preserving actor and destination
explanation: The luggage becomes the passive subject while the porter and destination stay the same.

rationales.Our luggage was carried from the taxi by: From the taxi reverses the direction of the original movement.
rationales.Our luggage carried a porter to the taxi: This makes the luggage carry the porter, reversing actor and receiver.
rationales.Our luggage was carried to the taxi by a: The luggage becomes the passive subject while the porter and destination stay the same.
rationales.A porter was carried to the taxi with ou: This makes the porter a person being carried, which the original does not say.

sentence: Which sentence says who caused the windows to open?
setupText: Choose the statement that explicitly identifies a person as opening the windows.
taskText: Which sentence says who caused the windows to open?
text: Choose the statement that explicitly identifies a person as opening the windows. Which sentence says who caused the windows to open?
options: The windows opened during the break.
The windows were open when we arrived.
The windows were opened by the receptionist.
answer: The windows were opened by the receptionist.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-a2-2304:Explicit passive agency versus intransitive change and state
explanation: Were opened is passive, and by the receptionist names the person who caused the action.

Opened can describe the windows changing position without identifying a person who did it.
rationales.The windows were opened by the reception: Were opened is passive, and by the receptionist names the person who caused the action.
Were opening presents movement in progress without naming who caused it.
Were open describes a state; it does not identify who opened the windows.

sentence: This photo was ___ from the roof.
setupText: Choose the grammatically correct completion.
taskText: This photo was ___ from the roof.
text: Choose the grammatically correct completion. This photo was ___ from the roof.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-a2-2305:Irregular taken in a past passive
explanation: Taken is the past participle of take. Was taken describes the photo as the result of someone's action.

rationales.took: Took is simple past; the passive after was needs taken.
rationales.taking: Was taking would be active continuous and would make the photo the photographer.
rationales.take: Take is the base form, not the participle needed after was.
rationales.taken: Taken is the past participle of take. Was taken describes the photo as the result of someone's action.

sentence: Library books can ___ at either entrance.
setupText: Choose the passive form for this return option available to borrowers.
taskText: Library books can ___ at either entrance.
text: Choose the passive form for this return option available to borrowers. Library books can ___ at either entrance.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-a2-2306:Can plus passive be
explanation: After can, use be plus returned to say what borrowers may do with the books.

rationales.be returned: After can, use be plus returned to say what borrowers may do with the books.
rationales.return them: Return them is active and would make the books the returning agents while repeating them as an object.
rationales.being returned: Can takes the base form be, not being, before the passive participle.
rationales.are returned: Are cannot follow can; the required base form is be.

sentence: The winners ___ tomorrow evening.
setupText: Choose the form saying someone will announce the winners tomorrow.
taskText: The winners ___ tomorrow evening.
text: Choose the form saying someone will announce the winners tomorrow. The winners ___ tomorrow evening.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-a2-2307:Future passive with will
explanation: Will be announced is future passive and leaves the announcer unnamed.

rationales.will announce: Will announce makes the winners the announcers, rather than the people whose names are announced.
rationales.will announcing: Will cannot directly take announcing; this passive needs will be announced.
rationales.will be announced: Will be announced is future passive and leaves the announcer unnamed.
rationales.have announced: Have announced describes a completed active announcement by the winners, not a future announcement about them.

sentence: The wood was cut ___ a carpenter ___ a hand saw.
setupText: Choose the words identifying the worker and the tool correctly.
taskText: The wood was cut ___ a carpenter ___ a hand saw.
text: Choose the words identifying the worker and the tool correctly. The wood was cut ___ a carpenter ___ a hand saw.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-a2-2308:Agent by versus instrument with
explanation: By a carpenter names the doer, while with a hand saw names the instrument.

rationales.with / by: By identifies the carpenter who acts; with identifies the tool used. This pair reverses those roles.
rationales.by / with: By a carpenter names the doer, while with a hand saw names the instrument.
rationales.from / by: From does not identify the acting carpenter, and by a hand saw does not give the requested tool phrase here.
rationales.by / from: By correctly names the carpenter, but from presents a source rather than the cutting tool.

sentence: The paintings were donated by ___.
setupText: Choose the grammatically correct completion.
taskText: The paintings were donated by ___.
text: Choose the grammatically correct completion. The paintings were donated by ___.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-a2-2309:Plural object pronoun in a passive agent phrase
explanation: Them is the object pronoun after by and identifies the people who donated the paintings.

rationales.they: They is a subject pronoun; after by use them.
rationales.their: Their needs a following noun, such as their family; it cannot stand alone here.
rationales.theirs: Theirs expresses possession rather than naming the donating people in this sentence.
rationales.them: Them is the object pronoun after by and identifies the people who donated the paintings.

sentence: Ask when someone repaired the bridge, starting with 'When'.
setupText: Choose the neutral direct question with the helping verb before the subject.
taskText: Ask when someone repaired the bridge, starting with 'When'.
text: Choose the neutral direct question with the helping verb before the subject. Ask when someone repaired the bridge, starting with 'When'.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-a2-2310:Past passive wh-question order
explanation: In a direct past passive question, place 'was' before 'the bridge' and 'repaired' after it.

rationales.When was the bridge repaired?: In a direct past passive question, place 'was' before 'the bridge' and 'repaired' after it.
rationales.When did the bridge repaired?: 'Did' cannot directly combine with 'repaired' to make a passive question.
rationales.When was repaired the bridge?: The subject belongs between 'was' and 'repaired' in this direct question.
rationales.When the bridge was repaired?: This is embedded-question order; the direct question needs 'was' before 'the bridge'.

sentence: The invitations were sent to the residents by the town hall staff.
setupText: Choose the meaning of 'to the residents'.
taskText: The invitations were sent to the residents by the town hall staff.
text: Choose the meaning of 'to the residents'. The invitations were sent to the residents by the town hall staff.
options: It names who sent the invitations.
It gives the place where the invitations were printed.
It names who received the invitations.
It says who wrote the invitations.
answer: It names who received the invitations.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-a2-2311:Recipient to versus agent by in a passive
explanation: 'To the residents' identifies the recipients. 'By the town hall staff' identifies the senders.

The senders are named after 'by', not after 'to'.
rationales.It gives the place where the invitations: The phrase identifies people receiving invitations, not a printing location.
'To the residents' identifies the recipients. 'By the town hall staff' identifies the senders.
Writing and sending are different actions, and this sentence does not identify the writer.

sentence: At this factory, the beans ___ and then ___ into bags.
setupText: Choose the pair that keeps the coffee beans as receivers in both steps.
taskText: At this factory, the beans ___ and then ___ into bags.
text: Choose the pair that keeps the coffee beans as receivers in both steps. At this factory, the beans ___ and then ___ into bags.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-a2-2312:Parallel passives in a simple process description
explanation: Are roasted and are packed keep the beans as receivers of both factory actions.

rationales.roast / pack: Both active forms make the beans the doers rather than the things processed.
rationales.are roasted / are packed: Are roasted and are packed keep the beans as receivers of both factory actions.
rationales.are roasting / pack: Are roasting is active continuous, and pack is active; neither gives the requested two passive steps.
rationales.roast / are packing: The active forms do not express workers performing both operations on the beans.

sentence: Phones must ___ during the performance.
setupText: Choose the form expressing a rule about what users must do to their phones.
taskText: Phones must ___ during the performance.
text: Choose the form expressing a rule about what users must do to their phones. Phones must ___ during the performance.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-a2-2313:Must plus a phrasal passive
explanation: Must be switched off is a passive obligation: users must switch off their phones.

rationales.switch off them: Switch off them is an active phrase with incorrect pronoun placement and makes phones the actors.
rationales.be switching off: Be switching off is active continuous; the rule concerns people switching the phones off.
rationales.have switched off: Have switched off is active perfect, not the passive instruction about what must happen to phones.
rationales.be switched off: Must be switched off is a passive obligation: users must switch off their phones.

sentence: Someone stole my wallet. I do not know who did it.
setupText: Choose the sentence that reports the theft without inventing the thief's identity.
taskText: Someone stole my wallet. I do not know who did it.
text: Choose the sentence that reports the theft without inventing the thief's identity. Someone stole my wallet. I do not know who did it.
options: My wallet was stolen by a passenger.
My wallet was lost on the bus.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-a2-2314:Agent omission when the doer is unknown
explanation: The passive reports what happened to the wallet and leaves the unknown thief unnamed.

The passive reports what happened to the wallet and leaves the unknown thief unnamed.
A passenger is an unsupported identification; the source says the thief is unknown.
This makes the speaker the thief and changes whose wallet was taken.
Losing something is not the same as someone stealing it, and no bus location was supplied.

sentence: Most of the rice ___ grown near the river.
setupText: Choose the grammatically correct completion.
taskText: Most of the rice ___ grown near the river.
text: Choose the grammatically correct completion. Most of the rice ___ grown near the river.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-a2-2315:Uncountable agreement in a present passive
explanation: Rice is treated as singular, so most of the rice is grown forms the passive correctly.

rationales.are: Rice is uncountable here and takes singular is, even after most of.
rationales.have: Have grown is active and does not agree with the uncountable subject in this statement.
rationales.is: Rice is treated as singular, so most of the rice is grown forms the passive correctly.
rationales.do: Do cannot combine directly with grown to form this passive.

sentence: The airline canceled Flight 208 because of snow.
setupText: Choose the sentence that keeps the flight as the main topic and reports the same event.
taskText: The airline canceled Flight 208 because of snow.
text: Choose the sentence that keeps the flight as the main topic and reports the same event. The airline canceled Flight 208 because of snow.
options: Flight 208 canceled the airline because of snow.
Flight 208 was canceled because of snow.
Snow was canceled by the airline on Flight 208.
Flight 208 was delayed because of snow.
answer: Flight 208 was canceled because of snow.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-a2-2316:Receiver-focused news with omitted recoverable agent
explanation: Was canceled keeps Flight 208 as the topic and preserves both the event and its stated cause.

rationales.Flight 208 canceled the airline because: This wrongly makes the flight the actor canceling the airline.
Was canceled keeps Flight 208 as the topic and preserves both the event and its stated cause.
rationales.Snow was canceled by the airline on Flig: Snow is the cause, not something the airline canceled.
Delayed means postponed, which does not preserve the stronger original event canceled.

sentence: You can see the tool but do not know its English name.
setupText: Choose the question asking for this tool's name.
taskText: You can see the tool but do not know its English name.
text: Choose the question asking for this tool's name. You can see the tool but do not know its English name.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-a2-2317:Passive question for an unknown name
explanation: What is this tool called? asks what name people use for the tool.

rationales.What does this tool call?: This makes the tool the caller and does not ask what people name it.
rationales.Who calls this tool?: Who asks about a caller, not about the tool's name.
rationales.What is this tool calling?: Is calling describes an active calling action, not a name.
rationales.What is this tool called?: What is this tool called? asks what name people use for the tool.

sentence: A customer asks what the ring is made of.
setupText: Choose the statement identifying the ring's material.
taskText: A customer asks what the ring is made of.
text: Choose the statement identifying the ring's material. A customer asks what the ring is made of.
options: It is made by a local artist.
It is made in a small workshop.
It is made for a visitor.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-a2-2318:Material versus maker, location, and beneficiary after made
explanation: Made of silver identifies the material composing the ring.

Made of silver identifies the material composing the ring.
By a local artist identifies the maker, not the material.
In a small workshop gives the place of production.
For a visitor identifies the intended recipient, not what the ring consists of.

sentence: The gate will be repaired by Thursday by our caretaker.
setupText: Choose the phrase that identifies the person doing the repair.
taskText: The gate will be repaired by Thursday by our caretaker.
text: Choose the phrase that identifies the person doing the repair. The gate will be repaired by Thursday by our caretaker.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-a2-2319:Agent by distinguished from deadline by
explanation: By our caretaker identifies the agent because it names the person carrying out the repair.

rationales.The gate: The gate is the thing repaired, not the person doing the work.
rationales.By Thursday: By Thursday gives a deadline; by does not always introduce a person.
rationales.By our caretaker: By our caretaker identifies the agent because it names the person carrying out the repair.
rationales.Will be repaired: Will be repaired is the passive action phrase; it does not identify the worker.

sentence: The tickets ___ online yesterday; customers had to buy them at the door.
setupText: Choose the form meaning no tickets were sold through the website yesterday.
taskText: The tickets ___ online yesterday; customers had to buy them at the door.
text: Choose the form meaning no tickets were sold through the website yesterday. The tickets ___ online yesterday; customers had to buy them at the door.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-a2-2320:Past passive negation with a restricted sales channel
explanation: Weren't sold is a past passive negative. It denies online sales while allowing sales at the door.

rationales.didn't sell them: Didn't sell them makes tickets the sellers and repeats them as an object.
rationales.weren't sold: Weren't sold is a past passive negative. It denies online sales while allowing sales at the door.
rationales.weren't selling them: Weren't selling them is active continuous and makes the tickets act as sellers.
rationales.hasn't sold: Hasn't sold is active, singular, and present perfect; it does not express the dated plural passive negative.
